 Daily Stock Market Live
 Live Updates Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 5:01 AM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Nasdaq-100 futures fall over 1% as Alphabet shares sell off after earnings report: Live updates
 Hugh Leask Justina Lee Paulina Likos Screens display the Fed rate announcement as traders work on the floor of the NYSE in New York City, US, Oct. 28, 2026. Jeenah Moon | Reuters Nasdaq-100 futures shed 1.21% early Thursday as investors digested the latest round of hyperscaler earnings.
 Dow Jones futures added 198 points, or 0.38%, while futures tied to the broad-based S&P 500 dipped 0.39%
 Alphabet was down 10.38% in premarket trading after it missed expectations on adjusted earnings per share and revenue in the third quarter. The Google parent posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. The company kept its full-year capital expenditures forecast at $195 billion to $205 billion.
 In contrast, Microsoft was up 3.73% in premarket trade, after growth in the software giant's Azure cloud infrastructure business helped it post beats on the top and bottom lines in the fiscal first quarter, per LSEG.
 Neoclouds fell as Microsoft's lower-than-expected capital expenditures figure pointed to infrastructure partners taking longer to deliver data center capacity.
 The results come as the artificial intelligence trade is in focus. AI stocks, such as the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) , have been through a rough patch for most of October, only to perk up in recent days.
 In Asia, Japan's  Nikkei 225  closed 1.10% higher. South Korea's Kospi fell 1.24%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 ended 0.5% higher. Mainland China's CSI 300 closed 1.03% higher. 
 Chips helped lift the broader market to a winning regular session on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 rising for a third straight day as Micron Technology jumped almost 6% and Broadcom added more than 2%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite also eked out a gain, advancing 0.3%.
 Earlier Wednesday, the Federal Reserve decided to hold steady on rates , leaving the central bank's benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75% and 4%. The decision to hold was widely expected as the Federal Open Market Committee issued a quarter-percentage-point hike in September. 
 This time, central bank policymakers pointed out that inflation "remains elevated," but also said that it was awaiting the "accumulation of more information" before it takes further steps.
 The Fed's decision "can be interpreted as mildly dovish at the margin, but we think it is better viewed as an expression of patience rather than a shift away from a tightening bias," said Daniel Siluk, head of global short duration and liquidity at Janus Henderson Investors. "The door remains open to further tightening, but the Committee appears willing to wait for incoming data to validate the need for additional action."
 Traders will get further insight into the economy on Thursday, when the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index report for September comes out. The PCE is a preferred inflation gauge for the Federal Reserve. The first reading of third-quarter GDP and weekly jobless claims are also due.
 On the earnings front, all eyes will be on quarterly reports from Caterpillar and Eli Lilly in the morning, followed by Amazon and Intel after the market close.
 12 Min Ago Shell pops 3% as profit nearly doubles to top expectations
 London-listed shares of Shell were 3% higher at an all-time high in morning trade after the oil major reported better-than-expected profit and record refining margins in the third quarter. 
 Adjusted earnings, the company's measure of net profit, rose to $10.81 billion from $5.43 billion a year ago, ahead of the $9.92 billion forecast in an LSEG-compiled consensus. 
 Elevated commodity prices and global tightness in refined products meant the company also announced hiked its quarterly share buyback program to $5 billion from £3 billion.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Shell share price. — Jenni Reid 
 13 Min Ago Volkswagen sees over $6 billion loss as Chinese market weakness
 German automaker Volkswagen recorded a more-than $6 billion loss in its third quarter , amid Chinese market weakness and U.S. tariff costs. 
 The Porsche and Audi owner on Thursday posted an operating loss of nearly 5.9 billion euros ($6.6 billion), while sales revenue also tanked 6.3% to 75.3 billion euros.
 The company recorded 8.7 billion euros in special items, mostly write-downs, with 6.4 billion euros related to Porsche Goodwill and about 1 billion euros on assets in China, as well as costs tied to the planned sales of its Osnabrück plant. 
 "The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively," Volkswagen's Chief Financial and Chief Operating Officer Arno Antlitz said in the report. 
 Antlitz said the results were affected by costly U.S. tariffs, a shrinking market in China, and a significant increase in competitive pressure in Europe. 
 "After nine months, our operating return on sales before special items stands at 3.8 percent. That is too low to continue investing strongly in our future," he added. 
 The company has forged ahead with its restructuring program, with announcements this year that it plans to slash 100,000 jobs in total . 
 Volkswagen was trading below the flatline after the opening bell and is down 34% so far this year. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Volkswagen shares since the beginning of this year. Volkswagen is forecasting group sales revenue in 2026 of around 315 billion euros for the full year. 
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 49 Min Ago Carlsberg beer sales continue decline as young and old moderate their alcohol consumption 
 Danish Brewer Carlsberg reported a decline in beer sales on Thursday, as consumers across "all generations" moderated their alcohol habits, its CEO told CNBC. 
 The beverage giant reported that its third-quarter volume grew 5% overall, with soft drinks up 9% and alcohol-free brews rising 11%. However, its premium beer sales declined 3%. The company said revenue grew 5% to 25.3 billion Swedish Kronor ($2.5 billion).
 "People are not leaving alcohol, but they are moderating within the category. So they are switching more between alcoholic and non-alcoholic products," Carlsberg's CEO Jacob Aarup-Andersen told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Thursday.
 watch now VIDEO 3:14 03:14 Carlsberg CEO: All generations are moderating alcohol consumption Squawk Box Europe "What we are seeing is that all generations are moderating... we all talk about the young generations here, but actually, it's you and me." 
 Carlsberg also saw a 6.7% volume decline in Asia, which Aarup-Andersen attributed to a "subdued consumer" in China as well as severe weather across the summer, which impacted beer sales. Aarup-Andersen also said that the European consumer is sensitive to costs and looking for better value. 
 "Beer and generally beverages is a very resilient category...this is not a luxury good. People see it as an everyday staple," he said. "But of course there is a price sensitivity, especially in lower mainstream... and across Europe we see affordability as a real issue."
 The company maintained its full-year forecast with operating profit expected to grow between 4% and 6%. 
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 1 Hour Ago European stock markets open the session in the green
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 was up 0.11% shortly after 8:10 a.m. in London (4:10 a.m. E.T.) with regional sectors and major bourses mostly higher.
 The French CAC 40 advanced 0.67% in Paris. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was up 0.27% in London, while in Frankfurt, Germany's DAX moved 0.21% higher. In Milan, Italy's FTSE MIB was down 0.43%.
 Chemicals added 0.97%, and household goods rose 0.91%. The continent's oil and gas companies rose 0.94%, aided by Shell 's 1.7% advance in early trade, after the U.K. energy major doubled its quarterly profits year-on-year. 
 Europe's banks led losses, down 1.08%. Autos and parts dipped 0.49%, with Volkswagen sliding 1.7% after the opening bell after reporting sharp operating losses in the third quarter. Tech companies fell 0.46%.
 — Hugh Leask 
 1 Hour Ago Japan's Nikkei rises 1.1%, South Korea's Kospi falls 1.2%
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  closed 1.10% higher at 64,659.47,  while the Topix gained 0.29% to 4,003.28.
 South Korea's Kospi fell 1.24% to 5,937.66 and the tech-focused, small-cap Kosdaq declined 2.34% at 753.23.
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 ended 0.5% higher at 8,891.80.
 Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  was up 0.24% in its last hour of trade, while mainland China's CSI 300 closed 1.03% higher at 4,041.84.
 — Justina Lee 
 2 Hours Ago Renault affirms full-year outlook despite a 6% slide in third-quarter car sales 
 French carmaker Renault is maintaining its full-year outlook on Thursday despite seeing a 6% drop in third-quarter car sales.
 The company reported Thursday that third-quarter group sales fell to 497,799 vehicles due to a "backdrop of fierce competition," while auto revenues stayed flat at 9.8 billion euros ($10.9 billion). The company attributed declining sales to challenging conditions in Turkey and Latin America, particularly Argentina. 
 Despite this, revenues rose 1.5% to 11.6 billion euros as sales of electric vehicles jumped 84.7% year-on-year and accounted for just over a quarter of passenger cars sold. The company's shares have declined 25.6% since the beginning of the year.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Renault shares since the beginning of the year. "Renault Group delivered resilient Q3 revenue, once again demonstrating the strength and agility of our operating model," Renault's chief financial officer, Duncan Minto, said in the report. 
 "This agility was particularly evident in Q3 as we successfully adapted to Europe's fast-shifting energy mix, leveraging our dual EV and hybrid strategy along with the efficiency of our manufacturing & supply chain setup."
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 7 Hours Ago Samsung Electronics third-quarter profit in line with estimates amid rising demand for AI memory chips
 South Korean tech giant Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported third-quarter operating profit that is broadly in line with analysts' expectations, as demand for advanced memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications continued to grow.
 Samsung's revenue rose 126.88% year-on-year and 13.85% from the previous quarter, while operating profit rose 783.11% from a year earlier.
 During the third quarter, Samsung Electronics and five of its affiliates announced a combined $1 billion investment in KKR-backed Helix Digital Infrastructure. Samsung Electronics will invest $500 million, with the remaining amount coming from its affiliates.
 Samsung has also announced a partnership with French AI startup Mistral AI to use AI technologies in its semiconductor operations, including chip design and manufacturing. The company also led Mistral's Series D funding round.
 — Jenny Lee 
 8 Hours Ago Mainland China and Hong Kong shares open mixed 
 Mainland China and Hong Kong shares were mixed, tracking other Asian markets as investors continue to digest the latest round of earnings. 
 Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  rose 0.24%, while mainland China's CSI 300 declined 0.64%. 
 The gains in Hang Seng were led by healthcare and energy sectors, up 1.64% and 0.45%, respectively. 
 — Justina Lee 
 8 Hours Ago Advantest's shares surges 8% after company raises outlook 
 Shares of Advantest rose more than 8% after the semiconductor test solutions provider raised its full-year outlook on expectations that robust market conditions would continue into 2027. 
 Net income for the second quarter ended September was at 193.3 billion yen, compared with 79.6 billion yen in the same period a year ago. 
 Net sales in the quarter also surged by more than 81% on-year to 477.7 billion yen, driven by strong demand for semiconductor testing equipment linked to AI applications.
 "Barring geopolitical risks and macroeconomic factors, we expect the industry to remain supply constrained, with end-customer demand continuing to exceed supply in CY27," the company said in its earnings presentation after market hours on Wednesday. 
 — Justina Lee 
 9 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei gains 0.6%, South Korea's Kospi inches higher
 Asia-Pacific markets traded broadly higher early Thursday. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  added over 0.58% while the Topix was flat.
 The Kospi rose 0.11% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq fell 0.97%. 
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.51% higher.
 —Justina Lee 
 10 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to open higher after U.S. Fed holds rates steady 
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open broadly higher Thursday, tracking U.S. stocks after the U.S. Fed holds steady on rates. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  was poised to rise, with the Chicago futures contract at 64,595 and its Osaka counterpart last trading at 64,360, compared with the index's previous close of 63,954.19.
 Hong Kong  Hang Seng index  futures were at 23,103, compared with the index's last close of 23,094.83.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 0.47% higher. 
 Worries over the Middle East war continue to linger. According to the Wall Street Journal , the U.S. has conveyed to Gulf Arab countries to get ready for a intense, short military campaign following the U.S. midterm elections. 
 —Justina Lee 
 10 Hours Ago ServiceNow and other stocks moving in after-hours trading
 Shares of ServiceNow plummeted 18% in extended hours trading Wednesday after reporting its third quarter. 
 The enterprise software company posted adjusted profit of $1 per share, missing the LSEG consensus expectation of $1.02 a share. 
 Meanwhile, subscription revenue guidance for the fourth quarter ranged from $4.245 billion to $4.255 billion, while the FactSet consensus called for $4.25 billion. 
 Other stocks moving in extended trading include Chipotle Mexican Grill , Fortinet and Sprouts Farmers Market .
 — Paulina Likos 
 11 Hours Ago Lumentum shares rise on Bloomberg report that Marvell is in talks to buy optics player
 Shares of optics maker Lumentum jumped in extended trading after Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar, that Marvell Technology is in talks to buy the company.
 An acquisition could be announced as early as next week, the people told Bloomberg. These people also told Bloomberg that the details could still change and that a final agreement hasn't yet been reached.
 Lumentum shares surged 11% on the report, while chipmaker Marvell lost more than 8%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Lumentum and Marvell in the past day In the artificial intelligence trade, Lumentum has emerged as a winner in the infrastructure space. The company builds optical transceivers and the photonic technology underlying AI and data centers. Shares have surged almost 148% in 2026 alone. In that period, Marvell has rocketed almost 200%.
 — Darla Mercado 
 11 Hours Ago Amazon set to report third-quarter earnings Thursday evening
 Big Tech earnings will continue Thursday with third-quarter results set to come from Amazon after the close. 
 The Street expects revenue of $202.22 billion, slightly above the high-end of the $197 billion-$202 billion guidance range, according to FactSet.
 Investors will be keying in on growth in its cloud computing business, Amazon Web Services. Consensus estimates call for AWS revenue growth of 37.8% year over year, up from last quarter's 36.8% increase, according to FactSet.
 The market will also look at whether there is growing adoption of its custom Trainium chips. Amazon stock is up 10% so far in 2026.
 — Paulina Likos 
 11 Hours Ago S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq-100 futures open lower
 Futures tied to the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100 opened lower Wednesday night in New York.
 S&P 500 futures fell 0.3% and Nasdaq-100 futures lost 0.8% shortly after 6 p.m. Dow futures were initially up 47 points.
 -- Darla Mercado
